props.gloss_en: the mishna: a midwife who reached in and touched a fetus dead in its mother's womb is impure with seven-day impurity
Rabba: swallowed (encapsulated) impurity does not defile
Rabba: so too swallowed (encapsulated) purity does not become impure
the stam: swallowed impurity -- from Lev 11:40, 'one who eats of its carcass': even one who ate near sunset, and the Torah says he is pure
R' Yochanan: [a carcass's severe and light impurity] both last until it is unfit for a dog
bar Padda: a carcass's severe impurity [lasts only while it is fit] for a ger
a carcass's light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog (bar Padda; included in R' Yochanan's 'both')
an earthenware vessel with a sealed cover does not shield the impurity inside it from defiling
compressed impurity breaks through and rises to the heavens
an earthenware vessel with a sealed cover shields the purity inside it from becoming impure
Negaim 13:9: one who enters a leprous house with his garments on his shoulders and sandals and rings in his hands -- he and they are impure at once
Negaim 13:9: if he was wearing them, he is impure at once, and they are pure until he stays the time of eating a half-loaf
Mikvaot 10:8: one who swallowed an impure ring immerses and eats his teruma; if he vomited it, it is impure and renders him impure
Mikvaot 10:8: one who swallowed a pure ring, entered a corpse-tent, was sprinkled twice, immersed and vomited it -- it is as it was
the stam: Rabba spoke of one who swallowed two rings, one impure and one pure -- the impure does not defile the pure
Rabba: a fetus is different, since it will eventually come out
Shmuel: this impurity [of the midwife] is not from the words of the Torah but from the words of the Scribes
the stam: Shmuel's wording means: do not say [the mishna] follows R' Akiva only -- even per R' Yishmael they decreed impurity rabbinically
R' Akiva: [one who touches] a fetus in a woman's womb is impure
R' Yishmael: [one who touches] a fetus in a woman's womb is pure
Rav Hoshaya: [the rabbinic impurity] is a decree lest the offspring put its head outside the vestibule
the stam: [the decree does not reach the woman herself because] a woman senses [this] in herself
R' Yishmael: 'whoever touches in the open field' (Num 19:16) -- to exclude a fetus in a woman's womb
R' Akiva: ['in the open field'] is to include the grave cover and its supports
the stam: R' Yishmael has grave cover and supports as a received halakha
R' Oshaya: R' Akiva's source is 'whoever touches a corpse, of the life [benefesh]' (Num 19:13) -- a dead one inside a person's life is a fetus in a woman's womb
the stam: R' Yishmael needs that verse for a revi'it of blood from a corpse, which defiles -- 'the life of a person' is a revi'it of blood
R' Akiva: even a revi'it of blood coming from two corpses defiles in a tent
R' Akiva: from 'nor shall he come upon any souls [nafshot] of the dead' (Lev 21:11) -- two souls and one measure
